hook_text: Thabo is 1 m 32 cm. Lindiwe is 128 cm. 128 is a bigger number, so Lindiwe is taller. Right?
clip_script: Classroom in Kimberley, height chart on the wall. Thabo: 1 metre 32 centimetres. Lindiwe: 128 centimetres. Same unit first! 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so Thabo is 132 centimetres. Thabo is taller, by 4 centimetres. Now the tools. Ruler: start at 0, not the end. 4 little marks past the 7: 7 centimetres 4 millimetres. Tape measure: bends round a tree trunk. Trundle wheel: one click, one metre, 85 clicks along the field, 85 metres. Choose the unit, start at 0, write the unit, and compare in the same unit.
visual_style: Whiteboard height chart with two learners; a ruler zooming into the 7 cm mark; a trundle wheel rolling with click counters.
pacing: The height puzzle, the unit fix, then three tools in quick succession.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure five things at home, estimating first.
